tour.title: Vertical Architecture
tour.description: Start with the architecture decision record to understand why the Casca-inspired SMB lending proof belongs inside NodeRoom rather than in a separate product. It establishes the governed evidence lifecycle, subsystem ownership, synthetic evaluation fixtures, and the crucial distinction between local browser proof and authenticated production certification.

tour.title: Lending Domain Protocol
tour.description: The lending seed turns a locked restaurant working-capital fixture into NodeRoom-native state: documents, blockers, financial metrics, critical paths, proposals, receipts, and a decision-free review packet. This is the domain protocol introduced by the architecture document, and it keeps evidence lineage and human credit authority explicit from the beginning.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript domain builders can keep a workflow deterministic by deriving typed projections and receipts from immutable fixture inputs instead of allowing UI components to invent business state.

tour.title: Runtime and CAS
tour.description: Building on the domain projection, the room engine constructs the lending room and coordinates proposal review, traces, artifact changes, and compare-and-swap protected transitions. The shared RoomStore contract then presents the same collaboration vocabulary to React through in-memory and Convex-backed providers, which is the architectural seam for eventually moving the proven local journey into durable production state.
tour.languageLesson: A React context backed by a typed store interface separates UI composition from persistence. CAS guards require the caller's expected version to match current state, preventing a stale proposal from overwriting newer human work.

tour.title: NodeRoom Entry Surface
tour.description: App.tsx is the scoped entry point that recognizes the SMB lending route, chooses the appropriate store provider, and mounts the vertical as a native NodeRoom experience. It demonstrates that lending is a specialized room configuration and artifact workflow, not a parallel application shell.
tour.languageLesson: React composition keeps routing, provider selection, and feature mounting at the application boundary while domain logic remains in typed modules below it.

tour.title: Artifact and Proof UI
tour.description: The artifact panel renders the underlying work product and proposal surfaces, while the lending proof bar exposes verified evidence status and a byte-backed export-and-reopen action. Responsive styles keep that proof control reachable on desktop, tablet, and mobile, connecting the protocol's receipts to something a reviewer can inspect and operate.

tour.title: Protocol Verification
tour.description: The integration test exercises the governed sequence beneath the UI: request missing evidence, approve it, verify a source-backed submission, apply it through CAS, regenerate the packet, and retain immutable lineage. It also asserts the most important lending boundary from Step 2: the system prepares a human-review packet but does not make the credit decision.

tour.title: Browser Golden Slice
tour.description: The Playwright journey proves that the same sequence is operable through the rendered NodeRoom interface, including approval, evidence verification, download, hash-checked reopen, and local reload recovery. Its desktop, tablet, and mobile assertions extend correctness beyond unit state into the actual user-visible product path while checking console health and horizontal overflow.
tour.languageLesson: End-to-end tests verify contracts that component tests cannot: browser persistence, downloaded bytes, responsive reachability, and the absence of runtime console failures.

tour.title: Benchmark and Evidence
tour.description: The four-mode benchmark compares manual, chat-only, graph-agent, and memory-enhanced behavior on locked restaurant and held-out medical fixtures, scoring candidates only after they are emitted. The machine-readable receipt preserves raw runs and provider telemetry, while the Markdown report summarizes document recall, blocker accuracy, authority compliance, source coverage, and runtime without collapsing them into an unsupported universal winner claim.

tour.title: Proof and Production Boundary
tour.description: The QA receipt binds browser screenshots, hashes, gates, and protocol assertions to the exact locally verified slice, while package scripts make the benchmark and broader repository checks repeatable. Finish with the remaining-work ledger: it deliberately separates completed local proof from unfinished authenticated Convex persistence, production deployment, optional Neo4j projection, and Casca-facing publication work so the vertical cannot overstate its readiness.
tour.languageLesson: JSON proof receipts are machine-checkable evidence, while a Markdown execution ledger communicates scope and limitations to humans. Keeping both prevents a passing local demo from being confused with a production certification.
